::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Novr 24th 1858  
**From:** Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection, C0171: Box 29.
:::

My dear [Mr Coleridge](people/person_332.qmd)
I send you a Post Office order for £2 which is all I can very well do for this most melancholy case, as just before Christmas is not the time for my galleons to come in. If you will send me another paper, I will forward it to some of the Gibbses who might perhaps be able to do something for the poor family.[^1] I do not know of any one else to ask.

Thank you for your information about the [Melanesian fund](organizations/other_30.qmd), which I thought most satisfactory, for it would be very absurd to detain the money from securities equally good and more profitable.

I was very sorry to miss the [Abrahams](people/person_4.qmd) when they were in this neighbourhood lately but the [Kebles](people/person_798.qmd) saw them. [Julian](people/person_1624.qmd) and [his bride](people/person_1604.qmd) are with some of her relations at present and [my mother](people/person_1606.qmd) has just set off to Winchester to the confirmation of [her Godchild](people/person_968.qmd), one of the Moberlys.

Pray give my kind regards to [your daughter](people/person_1808.qmd) and believe me

Yours very sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: [William Gibbs](people/person_560.qmd) (1790-1875), of Tyntesfield and his nephew [Henry Hucks Gibbs](people/person_558.qmd) (1819-1907) were both connected to CMY through the Crawley family.
